title: Move Less, Retrieve Fast: A Retrieval-in-Memory Architecture for Language Models
problem: Retrieval-augmented language models (RALMs) suffer from substantial data movement and irregular access patterns during retrieval, limiting efficiency on conventional CPU/GPU architectures.
motivation: RALMs are increasingly deployed for knowledge-grounded inference, but retrieval bottlenecks (data movement and irregular memory access) prevent practical deployment at scale.
method: Rimast places compute directly on memory chips—3D-stacked processing-in-memory hardware—so data doesn't have to travel long distances. The software is designed to work with this hardware: it organizes data flow in hierarchical levels to reduce transfers, spreads data evenly across memory to avoid bottlenecks (skew-free mapping), and dynamically decides which retrieval operations run on which parts of the system (adaptive offloading). This approach handles the irregular, hard-to-predict access patterns that come with retrieval-augmented language models.
key_novelty: Rimast is the first processing-in-memory system (putting compute directly on memory chips) specifically optimized for retrieval-augmented language models, using hierarchical data flow and balanced data distribution to achieve 273× speedup over CPUs.
contributions: Hierarchical PIM architecture with retrieval-in-memory dataflow minimizing data transfer
Skew-free data mapping addressing irregular retrieval access patterns
Adaptive offloading strategies for dynamic RALM workloads
273× speedup over CPUs, 55× over GPUs, 2.41× over prior accelerators

metrics.speedup: 273× over CPU, 55× over GPU, 2.41× over prior accelerators
